blindSummary:
This state/province was the epicentre and last holdout of the country's wave of anti-LGBT local resolutions. It was one of five state/provinces in the country to adopt such a regional declaration (repealed in September 2021 only after a supranational body threatened to freeze its development funds), and a district administration within it held the country's final surviving such local charter until its repeal in an extraordinary session in April 2025 - six years after the phenomenon began. The mayor of this state/province's capital outright banned the 2019 pride march on security grounds; a court later overturned the ban and the march proceeded, but the executive intent to exclude a visible LGBTQ public presence is on the record.

The resolutions were never criminal statutes, but the repeal was extrinsic (outside funding leverage) rather than a change in local attitudes, meaning the de facto social climate that produced them persists. For a visitor, the practical exposure is being visibly trans at a public event in a small town here where the local authority resisted all external pressure until 2025.

This position sits clearly below the national average - well below a large central state/province that also carried a resolution at this level but produced neither a march ban nor a five-year institutional holdout. It is the deepest sub-national negative recorded in the country's files.
